newsitem.title: USA: Sept. same-store retail spending fell - Telecheck.
newsitem.headline: Sept. same-store retail spending fell - Telecheck.

text.p: Telecheck, a subsidiary of First Data Corp, said Monday that September same-store retail spending fell 1.5 percent over the same period last year.
The Southwest and the Midwest led with a 0.3 percent gain.

Oklahoma posted a six percent increase, Missouri rose 2.4 percent and Texas was down 0.8 percent, Telecheck said. Sales climbed 6.1 percent in Illinois and 3.2 percent in Minnesota but fell 3.3 percent in Wisconsin, 3.4 percent in Ohio and 4.5 percent in Michigan, the company said.
Mid-Atlantic sales rose 0.2 percent, with Pennsylvania climbing 6.3 percent, Telecheck said.
The Southeast fell 1.9 percent and the West was down 2.6 percent. Spending in the Northeast fell five percent, with New York up 2.5 percent and New York City spending up 6.6 percent.

The 1.5 percent decline for the month could be due to an early Labor Day that shifted spending into August, one fewer Saturday in this year's month compared with last year's and consumer concerns about personal debt, said Telecheck's senior economic advisor William Ford.
